model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms generated by the Mistralv0.2-Base language model, both in its base form and after fine-tuning on six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The horizontal axis, labeled "Per-specialty terms," lists the six specialties in order from left to right: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis, labeled "Negative log probability," is scaled linearly from approximately -22 to -27, with tick marks at intervals of 1. For each specialty, there are seven grouped bars: a light blue bar representing the base model, and six colored bars (light orange to dark brown) representing the model fine-tuned on each of the six specialties, including the specialty itself. The legend indicates that the fine-tuned models are color-coded by the specialty they were trained on: Cardio (light orange), Gastro (medium orange), Infect (darker orange), Neuro (light brown), Obstetrics (medium brown), and Pediatrics (dark brown). The chart shows that for each specialty, the model fine-tuned on that specialty (the dark brown bar) consistently achieves the lowest negative log probability (i.e., highest probability), indicating better performance in generating terms specific to that domain. The base model (light blue) generally performs worse than all fine-tuned models across all specialties. The bars are arranged such that for each specialty group, the fine-tuned bars are ordered by the specialty they were trained on, with the self-specialty fine-tuned bar being the shortest (lowest negative log probability). The chart is rotated slightly counterclockwise, giving a 3D-like perspective, but the data remains two-dimensional.
